## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind. After editorial screening, a manuscript is sent to three expert reviewers drawn from the Editorial Review Board and the wider community; a second editor is consulted at or beyond the second revision, and the handling editor decides. Source: https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/author-guidance/the-review-process/ (retrieved 2026-11-23); the older Wiley guidelines copy (2023-12-09) adds that editors are "not vote-counters" and the three reviews are advisory |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank for the regular route. For special issues, the 2023 guest-editor guidance says a desk-rejected paper may be redirected to the regular submission process only if rejected solely for lack of fit (Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09) |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No statement found on the pages read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | 2 to 4 rounds of revision per the journal (review-process page, retrieved 2026-11-23). SciRev n=1 accepted manuscript reports 6 rounds (https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-management-studies/) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Current pages: authors who received feedback before submission must list everyone familiar with the paper and their identity, because those people may not review it (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/submit-to-jms/submit-journal-articles/, retrieved 2026-11-23). The older Wiley copy (2023-12-09) said authors may suggest reviewers or a preferred handling editor, at the Editorial Office's discretion. Authors are also expected to review for the journal if asked (same older copy) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes. The journal announced its own AI policy in an editorial of January 2024, "Here, There and Everywhere: On the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Management Research and the Peer-Review Process" (https://doi.org/10.1111/joms.13045; the Crossref record confirms it introduces a new journal policy, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/joms.13045; the editorial text and its Table 1 were not read). The submission page points authors to that policy |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate, but a duty to declare: the manuscript guidelines require authors to be transparent and specific about AI use "in any form, including copy-editing, language and grammar", preferably in the data or methods section, and the cover letter must confirm compliance and acknowledge any AI use or state that none was used (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/author-guidance/manuscript-preparation-guidelines/ and https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/submit-to-jms/submit-journal-articles/, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory, detailed disclosure, including language editing; this pass's own rubric; the policy table was not read, so prohibitions inside it are not known) |
| **Summary** | Journal: declare all AI use in the manuscript and in the cover letter; a reference style for citing generative AI is given in the guidelines. Publisher (Wiley, page undated, retrieved 2026-11-23): authors must disclose AI use when submitting, naming tool and version, date, its role and the author's review; AI-edited photographs are not permitted; reviewers and editors must not upload any part of a submitted manuscript to AI tools (https://www.wiley.com/en-us/publish/article/ai-guidelines/) |
| **Source URL** | https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/author-guidance/manuscript-preparation-guidelines/ ; https://doi.org/10.1111/joms.13045 ; https://www.wiley.com/en-us/publish/article/ai-guidelines/ |

## Format

> Sources: the journal's own pages, read live on 2026-11-23 (manuscript preparation guidelines, journal-article submission page, JMS Says page), and the Wiley guidelines copy dated 2023-12-09 for details the live pages omit. Where they differ both are given. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Original articles (empirical or conceptual) and review articles through the regular route; JMS Says (reflective essays), Point-Counterpoints, special issues and "JMS Insights" posts through their own routes (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/submit-to-jms/). Review articles must offer a theory-driven synthesis with a conceptual framework or research agenda and a described review method (submission page). The 2023 Wiley copy also listed "Commentaries", then closed to submissions |
| **Word limit** | Original and review articles: 10,000-13,000 words is typical; the count includes tables, figures and references; supplemental material for review or online-only does not count; manuscripts over 15,000 words may be returned for reduction (live manuscript guidelines and submission page). The 2023 Wiley copy said 9,000-12,000 typically and over 15,000 may be returned, with the same inclusion of tables, figures and references. JMS Says: a 300-word proposal, then up to 3,000 words (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/submit-to-jms/submit-jms-says/). Point-Counterpoint: a brief outline emailed to the editorial office (live page); the 2023 copy gave 9,000-12,000 words for a Point and about 7,000 for a CounterPoint |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Partly: the guidelines say new submissions exceeding the stated length "without justification" may be returned for reduction, which implies a justified overrun is considered; the 2023 copy adds that allowable length is "often at the Editor's discretion" |
| **Abstract limit** | At most 200 words, double-spaced; 4 to 6 keywords in alphabetical order below it (live manuscript guidelines) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the word limit. The journal's own author-date style, with a listed format for each source type, including generative AI (live manuscript guidelines) |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed for review or online-only publication and excluded from the word count (live manuscript guidelines) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables use Roman numerals, figures Arabic; each on its own page at the end; no footnotes, minimal endnotes under the heading NOTES (live manuscript guidelines) |
| **Anonymisation and other submission rules** | Authors' names must not appear in the manuscript; a separate title page carries identifying details; avoid wording that reveals identity such as "in our previous work" followed by an author-name citation. The cover letter must explain the contribution to JMS with reference to specific JMS papers, confirm AI-policy compliance, explain any previously published use of the same data and list related articles, and list people already familiar with the paper (submission page). Double-spaced throughout. iThenticate overlap screening is applied (review-process page) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, stated by the journal: "articles must make a strong theoretical contribution", with meaningful new implications or insights for theory present in every article, whether derived from empirical work or conceptual synthesis; submissions should clearly signal the nature of that contribution in relation to existing management and organizational literatures. Source: Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09, https://web.archive.org/web/20231209205314/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14676486/homepage/forauthors.html; the live review-process page repeats that manuscripts lacking theoretical contribution, methodological rigour or engagement with the literature receive a decision letter with feedback (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/author-guidance/the-review-process/). Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** Each submission should explicitly signal its theoretical and, if relevant, methodological position and stay consistent with it; submissions should be written so that the journal's general readers can follow them even if focused on a specialised literature (Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09). The journal's "address practice" aim says practical lessons must be grounded in rigorous research (mission statement, same copy).
- **Cover-letter framing:** the cover letter must say how the manuscript advances debates in the journal and refer to specific JMS papers it builds on or responds to, or explain how it brings a new debate to the journal (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/submit-to-jms/submit-journal-articles/, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Content the journal says it does not publish:** empirical investigations based only on student samples, and research relying solely on models that simulate behaviour (agent-based modelling, game theory models); it also warns that design problems such as small samples or no controls for common method bias in survey research are hard to repair after the study (Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09).
- **Special issues:** annual proposal cycle with a 31 March deadline and live open calls (see Publication Frequency).
- **Consequences of ignoring it:** manuscripts that do not meet the criteria or are "too weak" (methodological flaws, missing literature, limited theoretical contribution) may be rejected at the editor's initial evaluation with feedback; the guest-editor guidance names beyond scope, fatally flawed data or method, lack of contribution, student samples and simulations as the common desk-reject reasons (Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09). The publisher's box prints a 6% acceptance rate of unstated period (copy 2025-05-29).

### Methodological Preferences

> Scores follow this pass's own convention, not an external standard: share of the 635 abstract records (2021-2026, Crossref) whose title or abstract matches the expression; 0 hits = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. The journal states that qualitative and quantitative methods are both welcome and that it is open to approaches from positivism to critical research; it ranks no method, so no row exceeds 3. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how reviewers judge it. The schema's rows were kept where they fit; where they do not fit a management venue, this is said. Expressions are in the register in the AI-Research Notes.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Qualitative case study | 3 | "case study" 41 of 635 (6.5%); "qualitative" 54 (8.5%); "qualitative-any" 135 (21.3%) |
| Ethnography / fieldwork | 2 | "ethnograph*" 20 (3.1%) (does not match "autoethnography") |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | "interview" 38 (6.0%) |
| Survey / quantitative analysis | 3 | "quant-designs-any" 111 (17.5%); "quantitative-survey-any" 51 (8.0%); "survey" 33 (5.2%); "regression/panel/econometric" 15 (2.4%); "endogeneity/instrumental/propensity" 15 (2.4%); "structural equation/mediation/moderation" 49 (7.7%); the journal names missing controls for common method bias in survey research as a design problem (Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09) |
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | "experimental" 49 (7.7%); the pattern does not separate laboratory, field and natural or thought experiments, so the share may overstate designed experiments |
| Archival / historical analysis (added row) | 3 | "archival/historical" 37 (5.8%); "longitudinal" 48 (7.6%) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | "autoethnograph*" 0 of 635. The journal's JMS Says section takes personal reflective essays (live page), which are not counted here |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | "theory-building-any" 104 (16.4%): "conceptual" 44 (6.9%), "theorizing" 56 (8.8%), "essay" 11 (1.7%) |
| Mixed methods | 1 | "mixed methods" 1 (0.2%) |
| Meta-analysis | 0 | "meta-analysis" 0 of 635 abstracts and 0 title hits in 809 records |
| Literature review articles (added row) | 2 | "review-any" (systematic review, literature review, meta-analysis, bibliometric, scoping review) 18 (2.8%); Review Articles are a stated article type (live submission page) |
| Formal simulation / agent-based / game theory (added row) | 1 | "simulation/agent-based/game theory" 1 (0.2%); the journal says it does not publish research that relies solely on such models (Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Observation from the 635 abstracts (Crossref, 2021-2026), matching the abstract text alone (not the title; recomputed 2026-11-23): 607 (95.6%) contain a first-person word (I, my, we, our), nearly all plural; 31 (4.9%) contain singular I or my. For comparison, title plus abstract gives 607 (95.6%) any first person and 39 (6.1%) singular; the 31 is abstract-only. Among 50 single-author records with an abstract, 30 use singular I or my and 39 use any first-person form. Newest examples: https://doi.org/10.1111/joms.70174 and https://doi.org/10.1111/joms.70194 (any first person), https://doi.org/10.1111/joms.70153 (singular). The guidelines say language suggesting the authors' identity should be avoided (live manuscript guidelines). Plural "we" may be a convention of collective authorship rather than a stance |
| **Expected density** | Length 10,000-13,000 words typical including tables, figures and references (live guidelines); no article-length statistics were gathered |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Abstract of at most 200 words; 4 to 6 keywords in alphabetical order (live manuscript guidelines) |
| **Writing style notes** | UK or US English if consistent; double-spaced throughout; no footnotes and a minimum of endnotes; the journal's own author-date style (live manuscript guidelines). The 2023 copy asks that articles be written so that general readers of management and organization research can understand the argument (Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09). Section order of articles was not sampled |
| **Authorship pattern** | Crossref author counts over 809 records (677 list authors): 1 author 67, 2 authors 171, 3 authors 203, 4 or more 236 (retrieved 2026-11-23). Singly authored records are 9.9% of the 677 |

The Wiley copy of 2025-07-03 listed 339 | Live board page above; Wiley copy https://web.archive.org/web/20250703102304/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14676486/homepage/editorialboard.html |
| **Review model** | Double-blind, three reviewers, a second editor consulted from the second revision, reviews aimed within 3 months | https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/author-guidance/the-review-process/ ; retrieved 2026-11-23 |

No first-hand report beyond SciRev's n=2: the one full-process report rates report quality 4.0 of 5 and difficulty of comments 4.0 of 5, and says reviewers sometimes gave contradictory advice that the editor handled (paraphrased) | https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-management-studies/ |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Blank. The journal pages read (live guidelines, review process, submission page, and the 2023 Wiley copy) contain no ethics-approval, consent or IRB rule. The publisher's general ethics policy was not read; the live pages say the journal has been a COPE member since 2009 (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/about-jms/jms-ethics-metrics/, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are a minority: 67 of 677 Crossref records that list authors (9.9%), and 50 of the 635 records with abstracts (Crossref, 2021-2026). No rule limits single-author submissions on the pages read |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. No rule or count found; the pages read say nothing on unaffiliated authors. The society's funding page lists a British Academy scheme with a separate deadline for independent scholars, which is not a journal rule (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/sams/, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Journal-specific on reuse: authors using data they or their coauthors have already published must explain the new contribution and list every related article using the same dataset with similarities and differences; for widely used archival datasets only the most directly relevant prior work is cited (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/submit-to-jms/submit-journal-articles/, retrieved 2026-11-23). No open-data mandate found |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Each statement is attributed to the page that carries it (all read live 2026-11-23). The manuscript-preparation guidelines page (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/author-guidance/manuscript-preparation-guidelines/) supports two points only: author names stay out of the manuscript and go on a separate title page, and the text should avoid wording that suggests the authors' identities. "Double-blind" is stated on the review-process page (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/author-guidance/the-review-process/). The rule that people already familiar with the paper and the author's identity are "not eligible to act as reviewers", to be listed by the author, is on the journal-article submission page (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/submit-to-jms/submit-journal-articles/), in its cover-letter section. A preprint is allowed by publisher policy before submission (https://authors.wiley.com/author-resources/Journal-Authors/licensing/self-archiving.html) but the journal's stance on preprints is not stated |
| **AI use** | Any AI use, including copy-editing and language, must be declared in the manuscript and the cover letter (https://journalofmanagementstudies.ac.uk/publish/author-guidance/manuscript-preparation-guidelines/) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; APC not read (OpenAlex lists USD 4150 / EUR 3470 / GBP 2780, unverified); 492 of 855 works from 2021-2026 are hybrid open access in OpenAlex (https://api.openalex.org/works?filter=primary_location.source.issn:0022-2380,publication_year:2021-2026&group_by=open_access.oa_status) |
| **Other submission rules** | Resubmission of a manuscript rejected by an editor is not considered unless the editor invites a completely revised manuscript (Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09, https://web.archive.org/web/20231209205314/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/14676486/homepage/forauthors.html). The journal expects authors to review when asked (same copy). JMS Says authors must wait three years from acceptance before another proposal (live JMS Says page) |

### AI-Research Notes (sources, blanks, and cross-language checks)

**signal_quality (0-5)**: overall 3. Per layer: Crossref keyword counts (methods, topics, voice) 3 (809 records, 78.5% with abstracts, counts are lower bounds; the denominator includes front matter without abstracts); OpenAlex metrics and country counts 4; publisher-wide policies 3 (Wiley AI and self-archiving pages read directly but undated); journal-specific policies and guidelines 4 for the live journal site (read directly 2026-11-23) and 3 for the Wayback copies of the Wiley pages (2023-2025); experiential layer 1 (SciRev n=2, self-selected, no calendar dates).

**Per-subsection state (for the promotion gate)**: Epistemological, Framing, Methodological Preferences, Voice & Style, Reviewer Pool, Sensitive Topics and Practical Concerns rest on counts or journal text. Strong gaps: AI-policy table unread, ethics rules absent from the pages read, APC unread, preprint stance of the journal itself not stated, reviewer behaviour and review time beyond n=2 blank.

**Method.** Crossref records: `https://api.crossref.org/journals/0022-2380/works` (also via `works?filter=issn:0022-2380,from-pub-date:2021-01-01,until-pub-date:2026-11-23`, cursor paging, fields DOI, title, abstract, type, published, subject, author). 855 records: 809 of type journal-article (used) and 46 of type journal-issue (excluded); 635 of the 809 have abstracts. Abstract HTML tags were stripped. Each keyword was matched with a Python regular expression, case-insensitive, over title plus abstract, counting a record once; shares divide by 635. The two first-person expressions are the exception: they were run over the abstract text alone, not title plus abstract (recomputed 2026-11-23: 607 and 31 on abstracts alone; 607 and 39 on title plus abstract). Title-only counts run over all 809 titles. OpenAlex counts use group_by queries on `primary_location.source.issn:0022-2380,publication_year:2021-2026` (855 works), no key or email, single requests. The first-person expressions are case-sensitive: any first person `\b(?:I|[Mm]y|[Ww]e|[Oo]ur)\b`, singular `\b(?:I|[Mm]y)\b`. Board counts on the live site come from the HTML table rows of the Editorial Review Board and Strategic Advisory Board pages (last cell, Country, as printed) and from the Editors page's institution names; the Wiley copy's counts come from its list items (text after the last comma).

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Theory contribution**: the journal states every article must make a strong theoretical contribution and signal it in relation to the management and organizational literatures (Framing Requirements).
- **Excluded designs**: empirical work based only on student samples, or research relying solely on simulation or game-theory models, is not published (Framing Requirements; Wiley guidelines copy 2023-12-09).
- **Length**: 10,000-13,000 words typical including tables, figures and references; manuscripts over 15,000 words may be returned before consideration (Format).
- **Anonymisation and cover letter**: the manuscript must be anonymised, and the cover letter must connect to specific JMS papers, confirm AI-policy compliance, explain any reuse of published data and list people who have seen the paper (Format).
- **No re-entry after an editor's rejection** unless the editor invites a completely revised manuscript (Practical Concerns; older Wiley copy 2023-12-09).
- **AI**: any AI use, including language editing, must be declared in the manuscript and cover letter (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the journal aims for a first decision within three months and allows about four months per revision, with 2 to 4 rounds typical (Review Cycle Time). The only first-hand datum, SciRev n=1, is 37.3 weeks to acceptance over 6 rounds.
- **Selectivity**: the publisher's box prints a 6% acceptance rate of unstated period (Metrics).
- **Cover-letter work**: authors must reference specific JMS papers and list related articles on shared data (Format, Practical Concerns).
- **Preprint uncertainty**: publisher policy allows preprints, but the journal pages do not say whether JMS treats one as prior publication (Preprint Policy).
- **Open access cost**: gold open access carries an APC whose amount was not read (OpenAlex lists USD 4150 / EUR 3470 / GBP 2780, unverified; Open Access).

### Best Suited For

- Theory-driven empirical work in strategy, organization theory, international business, entrepreneurship, governance or organizational behaviour: "institutional" 13.9%, "corporate governance/ownership" 14.3%, "stakeholder/CSR" 13.2%, "top management/CEO" 11.0% of abstract records (Epistemological, Orientation).
- Quantitative designs with identification attention, and qualitative case or interview studies alike: "quant-designs-any" 17.5%, "case study" 6.5%, "interview" 6.0% (Methodological Preferences).
- Conceptual papers with a clear theoretical contribution: "theory-building-any" 16.4% (Methodological Preferences).
- Authors who can state their epistemological position explicitly, since the journal asks every submission to signal and maintain it (Framing Requirements).
- Short reflective essays through JMS Says, via a 300-word proposal (Format).

### Not Recommended For

- Student-sample-only or simulation-only studies: the journal says it does not publish them (Hard Blockers).
- Meta-analyses: 0 of 635 abstract records (Methodological Preferences); the count shows the form is absent from titles and abstracts, not that it is refused.
- Purely critical or post-structural work without a stated theory contribution: "Foucault*" 0, "Deleuze*" 0, "critical-management" 0.5% of abstract records (Epistemological); the journal says it is open to critical research, so this shows rarity, not rejection.
- Anyone needing a verified turnaround or acceptance rate before choosing: the 6% and 17-day figures are undated publisher labels (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).
